SCGSim takes a source model through backend preparation, explicit native
execution and a result report. Start with one small physical question and
follow it to the returned quantity before expanding the model.

## Getting Started

1. [Install SCGSim](course/installation.qmd) and the Python tools for your chosen
   backend. Native Palace or AEDT is installed separately on the solver host.
2. [Extract a pad capacitance](tutorials/capacitance.qmd): a square pad and
   surrounding ground, using Palace Electrostatic or Q3D.
3. [Find a resonance and read EPR](tutorials/resonance-epr.qmd): add an explicit
   inductive branch and use Palace or HFSS Eigenmode to read mode and
   participation quantities.

::: {.callout-tip title="Choose the backend where its procedure differs"}
The beginner lessons share source/model explanations and use tabs for the
backend-specific API steps. You can work in Python scripts or the public
OrPen notebooks; the notebook is a convenient execution interface.
:::

The starter setup and didactic controls now follow the owner's four canonical
SimplePad preparations: Palace Electrostatic, Q3D, Palace Eigenmode and HFSS
Eigenmode/EPR. Their [published source at `51985d9`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad)
and [downloadable notebooks](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad)
are linked by the lessons, with the shared layout picture and observed result
figures. The [public output context and data](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/evidence/README.md) accompany the
reference runs; the resonance lesson distinguishes the original HFSS return
from separately derived EPR. The Python blocks explain current SCGSim APIs;
the canonical notebooks remain OrPen's authority.

## Working with Your Model

[Modify your own model](course/working-model.qmd) explains Entity/Net assignments,
geometry changes and solver requests. [Inspect the source](course/source-observations.qmd)
and [prepared backend](course/solver-observations.qmd) when a model does not
match your intent. [Read returned results](course/returned-results.qmd) with
units, conductor/mode identity and the quantity your study needs.

Choose another physical task when appropriate:

| Task | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Ordinary port-free mode calculation | [HFSS Eigenmode](course/aedt-eigenmode.qmd) |
| Driven two-port response | [Driven Modal](course/aedt-driven-modal.qmd) or [Driven Terminal](course/aedt-driven-terminal.qmd) |
| Finite three-dimensional conductor matrices | [Q3D](course/aedt-q3d.qmd) |
| Per-unit-length line matrices | [Q2D cross sections](course/aedt-q2d.qmd) |

## Advanced

[Execute a portable handoff](course/execute.qmd) locally or with the selected
Palace Slurm profile. [Analyze sealed AEDT fields](course/aedt-saved-fields.qmd)
when the returned solution supports new EPR evaluation, or
[change loss assumptions offline](course/offline-epr.qmd) on recorded EPR data.
These are distinct operations with different native prerequisites.

The [Xmon source](tutorial-xmon-input.qmd), [Palace EPR](tutorial-xmon-palace.qmd)
and [HFSS EPR](tutorial-xmon-aedt.qmd) lessons retain the larger flip-chip
example, its literature adaptation and backend-specific geometry details.
They are deeper examples rather than prerequisites to the beginner course.

## Larger public examples {#public-inputs}

The deeper Xmon and CPW inputs below are pinned to OrPen source
[`35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9),
which declares OrPen `0.1.0` and GDSFactory 9.48.x. Use that model revision
when following these examples. The original notebook comments do not replace
the current SCGSim API reference.

| Canonical public notebook group | Use |
|---|---|
| [Kosen2024_Xmon](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon) | Palace Route A/B Electrostatic/Eigenmode and source-first Xmon studies |
| [ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround) | Ordinary HFSS Eigenmode, Driven Modal/Terminal and Q3D |
| [CrossSectionSimulation/CpwFiniteGround](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9/notebooks/src/CrossSectionSimulation/CpwFiniteGround) | Q2D rectangles and conductor groups |

The specimen dimensions and presets are public model inputs, not measured
process/device evidence. An old notebook's comments do not replace the current
package contract: for example, 3D Region padding uses the native
`(+X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z)` order, while Q2D uses `(-X,+X,-Y,+Y)`.


[Concept](concepts/problems.qmd) explains model choices and quantities;
[Contract](backend-support.qmd) provides the public API references. Repository
architecture and delivery information live in the [Maintainer guide](ownership.qmd).
